In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best performing methods for protein–protein interaction interface prediction are those that are able to identify a set of features that are optimal for the class of proteins under investigation.
the best performing method depends on the class and type of the protein under consideration.
no single predictor can be the best for all classes of proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed method is able to capture and discriminate the local surface patterns arising from different protein classes and is able to outperform the other state-of-the art interface predictors on the tested protein classes.
the 3D Zerneke descriptors, together with the SVM classifier, are able to capture and represent the complex protein recognition pattern and that they are a promising tool for interface recognition.
the 3D ZERNI interface predictor is able to capture the local surface patterns of the protein interface, but its usage is not optimal for every protein class.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3D Zermike descriptors are a promising tool for protein interface prediction, but that their usage should be coupled with a proper set of surface properties.
the 3D Zermike descriptors can be a useful and flexible tool for the interface prediction problem.

the 3D ZM descriptors are a powerful tool for the protein interface prediction problem, and that they can be easily used in combination with other descriptors to improve interface prediction accuracy.
